title: The Horse and the Stag
text:
Long ago the horse had a meadow all to himself and grazed it freely. Then a stag came along and began to feed in the same pasture, trampling the grass and eating his share.

The horse was furious and wanted revenge, but he could not drive the stag away on his own. So he went to a man and asked for help in punishing the intruder.

The man agreed, on one condition. The horse would have to let him put a bit in his mouth and a saddle on his back, and carry him. Then the man would take his weapons and deal with the stag.

The horse accepted the bargain. The man mounted him, and together they chased the stag out of the pasture. The horse had his revenge.

But when it was over, the man did not take the bit out of the horse's mouth or climb down. He rode him home, tied him in a stable, and kept him working. From that day on the horse was no longer free. To get even with the stag, he had made himself the servant of man.
lesson: Before asking a stronger party to fight your battle, ask what they will want afterward. The price of help can be your independence.
people: A horse, a stag, a man
